How far would
you go?
next_voice: Next, in Part Four: the stable.

beats.text: She sailed with a company of colonists bound for New France.
beats.scene: The empty deck of a seventeenth-century sailing ship at dusk, coiled ropes, a lantern, tall dark masts, heavy sails, a hard shaft of light across the wet planks, mist and a vast dark sea beyond the rail. Skewed angular painted-set architecture. No people.

beats.text: For a long time, there was only the sea.
The Vatican biography says she reached Ville-Marie on the sixteenth of November.
It was a small fort on an island, at the edge of a great forest.
beats.scene: A small wooden fort-town on a river island seen from the water at dawn: a log palisade, a few steep-roofed log houses, one small cross, a vast dark forest and drifting mist beyond, hard low light from one side. Skewed angular painted-set architecture. No people.

beats.text: There was no school yet, and no pupils.
beats.scene: A bare cold log hut in a snowy clearing at the edge of a dark forest, one small window with no light in it, empty snow, a lone fence post, a heavy sky, hard side light. Skewed angular painted-set architecture. No people.

beats.text: She had crossed an ocean to teach, and she would have to wait.
Years would pass before her first school.
